title: Act II, Scene IV

teacherSummary.text: Portia, nearly frantic with knowledge of the plot, sends the boy Lucius to the Senate house without being able to say why, then asks him to report how Brutus looks and who comes to Caesar. She questions the soothsayer, who plans to warn Caesar again from a narrow place in the street, and she nearly gives the secret away.

segments.script: Today's words: befriend — to help; to favor; commend — to send greetings; to recommend; suitors — people who bring a request; bustling — noisy and busy; constancy — firmness of mind. “suitors”: From Middle English sutour, from Anglo-Norman suytour, seuter, from Late Latin secutor "follower, pursuer".

words.sentence:
That I have, lady: if it will please Caesar
To be so good to Caesar as to hear me,
I shall beseech him to befriend himself.

Yes, bring me word, boy, if thy lord look well,
For he went sickly forth: and take good note
What Caesar doth, what suitors press to him.

O constancy, be strong upon my side,
Set a huge mountain ’tween my heart and tongue!
